tagline: Leading Nordic energy company powering sustainable future
hero_kpi_rationale: Gross Margin up 200 bps to 32%, reflecting optimization of the energy mix and lower production costs despite price volatility. Key indicator of profitability in the Nordic energy sector.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total sales generated by the company during the year.
kpis.description: Growth driven by energy prices and stable production. Strength of the Nordic energy portfolio amid increased demand.
kpis.signal: Revenue up significantly despite energy volatility.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.description: Improved cost efficiency and optimized energy mix. Sustained improvement in operating profitability due to better utilization of existing assets.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on new equipment or infrastructure.
kpis.description: Targeted investments in renewables and maintenance. Strategic commitment to the energy transition of the Nordic portfolio.
kpis.signal: Capex up to modernize the energy fleet.

kpis.name: Net Debt
kpis.explanation: Total financial debt minus available cash.
kpis.description: Solid financing structure despite moderate increase in leverage. Prudent capital management amid higher investment levels.

kpis.name: Return on Capital Employed
kpis.description: ROCE improving due to better asset utilization. Enhanced efficiency of capital employed in energy operations.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Lower production costs and sustained selling prices. Performance supported by improved cost control and favorable energy pricing.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 0.74 EUR in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of 1.256 Bn EUR in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Portion of net income distributed. >80% = potentially unsustainable.

kpis.name: Earnings Per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares during the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate earnings per share: basis for Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2020-2024). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Human rights risks in the supply chain
risks.summary: Fortum faces risks of human rights violations (forced labor, child labor, inadequate working conditions) in its global supply chain, particularly in solar component manufacturing and high-risk countries. Supplier qualification rate reaches only 81%, against a target of 85%.
risks.score_rationale: Recurrently mentioned in the supply chain section with moderate language ('potential risk', 'may be linked to'). Stable trend with corrective actions underway. Material category identified in the double materiality assessment.

risks.title: Impact of wind operations on indigenous peoples
risks.summary: Wind farms operated by a Fortum minority joint venture in Sweden and Norway affect traditional reindeer herding areas of indigenous communities. Fortum provides services to these facilities without direct control over operations, creating indirect exposure to litigation and reputational risks.
risks.score_rationale: Specific risk identified as a material negative impact in the double materiality assessment, linked to a joint venture in Sweden and Norway. Cautious language ('potential impacts', 'does not have control'). Stable trend, structural risk related to decarbonization strategy.

risks.title: Dependence on high-risk component suppliers
risks.summary: Fortum relies on critical materials (metals, minerals, solar components) whose supply chains present significant sustainability risks. The 2024 assessment covering 14 metals and minerals reveals gaps in risk management within procurement processes.
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly identified for 14 metals and minerals assessed in 2024, with acknowledgment that 'metals and minerals generally involve significant sustainability risks'. Trend increasing due to growth in renewable energy. Category weight significant for an energy transition company.

risks.title: Safety of subcontracted workers at operational sites
risks.summary: Safety incidents involving subcontractor employees at Fortum's operational sites constitute a material risk. Fortum manages this risk through safety committees, regular audits, and a Safety and Security Leadership Programme, but exposure remains significant due to the extent of the subcontractor network.
risks.score_rationale: Identified as a material negative impact (IRO S2.3) with strong language ('key priority'). Mentioned multiple times in the document with dedicated programs (Safety and Security Leadership Programme). Stable trend with active mitigation measures.

risks.title: Increasing regulatory compliance on due diligence
risks.summary: Fortum faces growing due diligence requirements across its supply chain (CSRD, duty of care laws). The supplier data assessment and management system is still under development until 2026, exposing Fortum to regulatory non-compliance risk in the interim.
risks.score_rationale: Implicit risk in multiple references to regulatory frameworks (UN Guiding Principles, OECD Guidelines, ILO). Supplier data management system not yet finalized (target 2026), indicating potential compliance lag. Trend increasing with tightening European ESG regulations.

risks.title: Social risks related to new energy site development
risks.summary: The development of new renewable energy production sites (wind, solar) exposes Fortum to conflicts with local communities and indigenous peoples over land use, noise, and landscape changes. These risks may delay or block construction permits.
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified as a medium-term negative impact related to development sites. Moderate language with preventive actions in place (screening tool). Trend increasing due to acceleration of renewable deployment in Fortum's strategy.

risks.title: Insufficient visibility on vulnerable workers in subcontracting
risks.summary: Fortum acknowledges limited visibility on migrant workers and other vulnerable groups in its supply chain. The absence of a system to verify whether reporting channels are accessible and used by value chain workers represents a reputational and compliance blind spot.
risks.score_rationale: Fortum explicitly recognizes 'limited visibility to vulnerable groups, such as migrant workers in the supply chain'. No tracking system for value chain worker reporting channels. Stable trend with corrective actions planned but not yet deployed.

ai_positioning.summary: Fortum does not mention any strategy or initiative related to artificial intelligence in the provided documents. The company does not position AI as a technological or operational lever.
evidence: No mention of AI in the Business, MD&A or Risks sections.
No references to automation, predictive analytics or optimization projects using AI.
Complete absence of AI-related vocabulary, machine learning or advanced data terms.
